how: A member proposes the Saltire and gives a starting location without needing proof that every reader joins.
Calls recruit hands for a located Saltire and ask for coordinated work.
Short replies commit to placing or confirm that another worker remains.
Questions about the canvas receive timer explanations and thanks, while the question about a pictured detail has no coded answer.
Members propose national emblems and revise the caption, thistle position and border rather than receiving one fixed design.
Builders report the Saltire in progress and divide work on its blue field and white cross.
Coordinates and updated designs tell helpers where to place and what to retain.
A posted console script invites automated whitening of the rival flag, without proving that readers ran it.
A reported timer bypass is not itself a script, spare account or verified enduring placement.
Members create and relink a planning chat and direct confused defenders there to recognize their own bottle construction.
Public referrals show where participants say planning happens but do not disclose the chat deliberation or all placers' access to it.
Members describe all-day watching and overnight five-minute repairs as personal contributions.
One member reports apparently unlimited placements disappearing and another claims a timer bypass without confirming persistent pixels.
Local task division assigns blue and white work without establishing a room-wide leader or formal government.
Members correct the cross, rally against damage and describe sustained daytime and overnight repair.
The shared-plan correction establishes a mistaken defence alarm, while actual erasure or loss of agreed changes remains untested.
Members distinguish their own faulty drawing from sabotage and identify an apparent takeover as their own new bottle.
Referring alarmed defenders to the planning venue supplies the explanation that the apparent intruders are their own builders.
Neighbours negotiate the menorah boundary and the local design becomes shorter to leave space.
Members accept a request not to expand and tell their own placers to respect neighbouring lettering.
Visitors speak for neighbouring works and bring boundary requests into the room.
Visitors offer protective pixels and members offer help defending neighbouring work.
Bilateral help is visible, but these passages do not establish a coalition or shared governing arrangement.
Negotiating adjacent boundaries does not establish one room hosting another under its jurisdiction.
Appeals to respect boundaries do not explicitly dispute or state who can bind every placer.
A proposed flag location is judged too large and repeated overwriting makes another start difficult.
Members compare starting sites before establishing a settled mark rather than only relocating after defeat.
A shorter design and a proposed caption move accommodate nearby work without a demonstrated total loss.
Early site choices and proposed caption moves do not establish completed relocation after an erased work.
A reply argues for doing independent work well rather than vandalising another flag.
An ironic reply challenges celebration by describing the displacement of a previously reasonable neighbour.
National belonging and independence enter both attack proposals and objections to politicising the art.
Members make canvas-specific jokes about naming the lion Katie and recruiting help for Nessie with three fiddy.
A reply jokingly suppresses mention of the unfinished lion in the celebratory account.
A joke receives a pointed answer, but no cited exchange establishes objection to offensive language or policing hate symbols.
A participant's Yes vote distinguishes political preference from artistic preference without establishing membership in both canvas rooms.
April Fools fakes make participants test news for joking and object to an entire front page of pranks.
Moderators pin coordination and later require canvas posts to stay in one thread under a deletion rule.
A new chat gathers an existing room's canvas effort around its flag rather than demonstrably creating a new independent collective.
Opening a coordination chat does not establish the recruitment of unknown repeaters or a new shared identity beyond the existing room.
Canvas containment and objections to April Fools posts do not connect a canvas-post protest to attacking the room's mark.
Members celebrate the flag, thank the night shift and describe pleasure in collective work.
The final image records the work after placement ends.
Members propose carrying cooperation into a cultural exchange and invite others to save the thistle elsewhere.
Adopting the work as a banner can be proposed during construction rather than only near or after closure.
An allied visitor enters the discussion through protective work, without demonstrating new subscriptions or recruitment growth.
An ally's exchange invitation evidences visiting and extending cooperation, not conversion into a lasting member or subscriber.
A post-event reply corrects the celebratory account by pointing out its omitted IndyRef label.
An ironic post-event correction disputes the account of harmless success without establishing an edited archival image.
A room caption and an allied exchange invitation do not establish outreach to depicted creators, companies or the press.
A repair complaint personally rebukes fellow builders for butchering the cross.
The harsh repair complaint shows personal strain but does not establish departure, apology or repaired relations.
Members call for erasing red from the rival flag and offer a console script to whiten it.
A hostile territorial rebuke addresses the national rival through the canvas contest.
A proposal to alter the rival flag explicitly promises the bonus of annoying British nationalists.
The same turn couples removing the rival flag's red with antagonism toward British nationalists.
Reporting observation of a rival chat does not establish planted spies, hidden plans or deliberate infiltration.
The proposed Saltire supplies the object and location around which the call asks members to coordinate.
A located recruitment thread receives a progress report and an explicit division of blue and white work.
A favourable progress report receives a reply instructing builders how to correct the existing cross.
Border talk anticipates mutually costly expansion rather than requiring demonstrated erosion inflicted by the neighbour.
A request to spare the menorah receives assent and a follow-up explaining that the redesign now leaves more room.
Reports of hostile scripts and a posted attack script do not establish local defensive automation caused by upkeep overload.
The staged construction proposal receives the same author's later report celebrating that the work was finally done.
Celebrations and a final image coexist without a cited request establishing that celebration caused the recording.
The banner proposal precedes the coded final image, so carrying the mark forward need not depend on that closing record.
The exchange invitation explicitly gives cooperation during the canvas as its reason for proposing a later cultural exchange.
Doubt about space and early site comparisons do not establish a shortage-driven move after loss.
An updated design retains the original thistle position after a proposed move rather than proving that every design proposal became agreed instruction.
A short acceptance joins a construction proposal without giving a reason or asking for a return.
An invitation to build the rival flags receives a bare refusal, so a reasoned decline is not mandatory.
Protective help appears under a repair appeal, but the quoted offer does not attribute it to a shortage of local hands.
Boundary requests and later protective help show sequence without identifying negotiation as the cause of that help.
The call to coordinate a Saltire receives a proposal to convert the rival flag instead.
A takeover call receives a reasoned preference for fixing the room's own cross first.
A proposed political alteration receives an answer grounding refusal in doing independent work well.
Attack proposals and neighbour negotiations concern different targets and do not establish an attack-to-deal transition.
An attack call and a later hostile address do not identify the particular attack as the cause of the taunt.
Offers of mutual help do not establish a coalition formed because local upkeep came under attack.
Scattered recruitment and construction posts are redirected into the pinned coordination thread and later subjected to an explicit containment rule.
An agreed border is visible without an explicit subsequent refusal of its authority or statement that placers cannot be bound.
